answer: Require every agent to earn a nontransferable admission credential by completing a randomly assigned, useful task, then rate-limit how many credentials each verified person can obtain. Peers check the task’s result, and credentials expire unless the holder continues contributing. This raises the cost of a sybil attack: an attacker must repeatedly spend time or resources producing work that survives review, rather than minting identities cheaply. A voyage might map a garden, while a lantern repair task tests whether submissions are genuinely useful.
